A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DGSWP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original transport-plan and gradient-flow experiments, plus CIFAR-10 conditional flow matching results, FID/NFE measurements and generated images in Section 5 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical studies and adds matched-runtime and Expected Sliced Transport Plans comparisons, alongside three-run summaries of the flow-matching results.

M1.justification: The bilevel objective, Gaussian smoothing, variance-reduced gradient estimator, Algorithm 1 and projection architectures remain unchanged. The new discussion of Python sorting and theoretical conditions clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic transport problems, Euclidean and hyperbolic gradient flows, and CIFAR-10 generation. The new Swiss Roll runtime comparison and EST experiments reuse existing data and tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix A.3.3 newly evaluates Expected Sliced Transport Plans (EST), previously only cited, at temperatures 0, 1 and 10. Table 3 compares it on 8Gaussians-to-Two-Moons transport, and Figure 7 compares it on two retained gradient-flow targets. Existing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New Table 2 compares min-SWGG and linear DGSWP under approximately matched runtimes, selecting different iteration counts for budgets from 3.34 to 13.33 seconds. The EST comparison introduces a temperature sweep. Previously stated training settings and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3.2 adds an analysis of whether DGSWP's convergence advantage survives matching computational time. A.3.3 examines EST temperature sensitivity. The earlier variance-reduction analyses remain, including v1 Figure 7 as v2 Figure 8.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Figure 6 newly report CFM averages over three runs with standard deviations; v1 supplied no CFM run count or uncertainty. This establishes changed reporting, not an explicit increase from a known earlier run count. Existing ten-seed gradient-flow reporting is retained.

E6.justification: CFM point reports are replaced by three-run summaries: for example, NN Euler FID changes from 3.56 to 3.62 ± 0.05, while Table 1 rankings remain unchanged. New results show min-SWGG winning at shorter matched budgets and DGSWP at longer ones. Table 3 adds EST costs of 32.28, 21.30 and 20.09 alongside retained DGSWP cost 13.80. Appendix A.3 newly reports I-CFM as approximately 25% faster than the other CFM methods.

T1.justification: Definition 2 changes the admissible exponent from p >= 0 to p > 1, and Section 3 explicitly requires a continuous projection map. Appendix A.2 adds an overall computational-complexity expression. The principal lemmas, propositions and Appendix A.1 proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same claims: generalized nonlinear transport plans, differentiable optimization, effective high-dimensional and manifold applications, and sliced-OT conditional flow matching. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that injectivity is required on the support, distinguishes defining the objective from proving metric properties, and acknowledges possible failure of Assumption 1 for ReLU networks. It also qualifies efficiency through the budget-dependent comparison and discusses EST's temperature-dependent performance.

D1.justification: v2 discloses reliance on Python's sorting order to select among minimizers and explains that aggregating ten minibatches was chosen to match OT-CFM runtime. It adds relative CFM runtime information. Existing architectures, optimizer settings, hardware descriptions and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bolte and Pauwels on conservative calculus and Tanguy, Chapel and Delon's Sliced Optimal Transport Plans. It expands comparison with the already cited EST work. Other reference renumbering and publication-metadata updates do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, expands explanations of injectivity and regularity, adds acknowledgments, and introduces dedicated appendix subsections for the new comparisons. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2–3 and Figure 7, adds standard-deviation bars to Figure 6, and enlarges and relocates Table 1. The original appendix Figures 7–9 are retained as Figures 8–10. These are localized display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The three-run CFM uncertainty reporting, direct EST comparisons and matched-runtime analysis improve empirical transparency and comparison fairness. The runtime analysis usefully exposes min-SWGG's advantage at short budgets, while clearer applicability caveats improve interpretation. These are focused improvements; the acknowledged ReLU regularity issue receives no corresponding new proof.
